name: mechanical back and neck pain overview
title: Mechanical back and neck pain: axial pain worse with movement and better with rest, with no red flags, sorted by the structure it comes from (disc, disc herniation, facet joint, muscle, whiplash); each column gives what tells it apart, investigations and treatment, with the rule for who to image below

nodes.title: Axial neck or back pain, WORSE with movement, BETTER with rest: which structure?
lines: pain generators: paraspinal muscle, soft tissue · disc · facet joint · nerves in the spine · sacroiliac joint
history with OLDCARS + red flags every time · exam: spine, contributing limb problems, neurological exam, red-flag signs
mechanical: midline or beside it · dull ache or sharp · degeneration, then 'tweaked' (stairs, a bad bend) · does NOT radiate to the tips of the limbs · NO red flags
any red flag → image now: see the NON-MECHANICAL chart · an exact anatomical diagnosis is often unnecessary

nodes.title: The DISC
lines: repeated loading → end-plate damage → tears in the anulus → disc loses height

nodes.title: The FACET joint
lines: a synovial joint: it gets arthritis

nodes.title: The MUSCLES
lines: no test proves it: investigate only to rule other things out

nodes.title: Discogenic pain
lines: internal disc disruption: nucleus pushes into tears, anulus INTACT

nodes.title: Disc herniation
lines: nucleus goes OUT through the anulus
bulge → protrusion → extrusion → sequestration
disc pain AND nerve compression

nodes.title: Facet (zygapophyseal) pain
lines: arthritis of the facet joint

nodes.title: Muscle
lines: • acute strain or spasm
• repetitive strain
• myofascial trigger points

nodes.title: Whiplash associated disorder
lines: acceleration-deceleration, e.g. car crash

nodes.title: Axial > leg
lines: • WORSE bending FORWARD (flexion)
• 20-40% of back pain

nodes.title: Younger · lifting · SUDDEN axial pain
lines: • WORSE with cough or sneeze
• goes posterolateral, toward the roots

nodes.title: Localized axial, ? one-sided
lines: • WORSE with EXTENSION, eased by flexion
• dull, achy · refers: headache, shoulder, leg
• neck → headache · low back: rarely past the knee

nodes.title: Movement-related, no red flags
lines: • repetitive strain: repetitive or forceful tasks, vibration, awkward postures
• trigger point: tender when pressed, can refer pain

nodes.title: Neck: MUSCLES most often
lines: less often: facets > anterior longitudinal ligament > bone > cord
most improve: < 5% severe at 2 years

nodes.title: No imaging at first
lines: see who to image, below

nodes.title: Uncomplicated: image only after
lines: a failed 4-6 week conservative trial

nodes.title: Imaging may not help
lines: facet degeneration does not match symptoms

nodes.title: No test diagnoses it
lines: rule out red flags; image only if concerned

nodes.title: More than pain, stiffness, ↓ range?
lines: • X-ray if fracture is a worry
• MRI if any neurological sign
• X-ray normal, pain still severe → CT (occult fracture)

nodes.title: Conservative
lines: • therapy (EXTENSION-based), exercise
• NSAIDs acutely, acetaminophen

nodes.title: Conservative first
lines: leg pain in a dermatome = radiculopathy: see the NON-MECHANICAL chart

nodes.title: 1 · Flexion-based therapy
lines: NSAIDs acutely, acetaminophen

nodes.title: 2 · ? Joint injection
lines: • only after therapy fails
• facet steroid injection · medial branch block
• radiofrequency ablation of the medial branch nerves: longer relief

nodes.title: Reassure: EXCELLENT prognosis
lines: • do NOT avoid movement
• relative rest, ice or heat, topicals
• short oral anti-inflammatory
• physiotherapy: postural support

nodes.title: Keep moving: NO collar
lines: • heat, ice · acetaminophen, NSAID
• MODEST physio: aggressive can worsen it

panels.title: Who to image (no red flags)
items: OVER 6 weeks DESPITE good conservative care → X-ray can be the starting point
imaging indicated → MRI is best · CT only if MRI is contraindicated or unavailable
imaging is often normal, and disc degeneration is common in adults with NO back pain
red-flag MRI: cancer, infection, cauda equina, severe or progressive deficit, compression fracture · URGENT for epidural abscess or hematoma

panels.title: Treating mechanical pain: the order
items: physiotherapy is the MAINSTAY, done routinely at home · most improve over time
acetaminophen, NSAIDs first · AVOID codeine and other opioids
facet injection only after therapy fails
surgery: axial pain WITH neurological symptoms only · purely axial pain does poorly

panels.title: Red flags → think of
items: neurological: progressive weakness, saddle anesthesia, incontinence, ↓ hand dexterity → cord or cauda equina
inflammatory: morning stiffness, better with exercise, 2nd half of the night → spondyloarthropathy
neoplastic: young, severe night pain, weight loss, cancer history · infection: fever, IV drug use, immunosuppression
fracture: trauma, osteoporosis · vascular: dizziness on neck movement (vertebral artery), claudication
